correctness.rationale: The code and full-rank eleven-check quotient are derived algebraically from affine interpolation on the binary 4-cube. A four-option Bellman recurrence enumerates all 2^22 pairs of syndromes and is proved by induction on the processed coordinates. The supplied C++17 checker executes this and, independently, enumerates every canonical coset pair and minimizes over all 32×32 affine row corrections. The two distances coincide state by state for all 4,194,304 cases, and the histogram adds to that total. A radius-nine witness and all 336 deepest classes are located. The finite proof does not claim any infinite-case classification.

originality.rationale: The exact ten-coefficient two-row coset-distance polynomial was not implied by any inspected primary result: the most relevant 2022 Reed–Muller Table I excludes r=1,m=4; 2026 general theorems give inequalities; and the ordinary deep-hole tables lack joint residual support. Aliases including F4 scalar extension and covering-code cosets were searched. A 2026 cyclic-code paper remains incompletely accessible; this risk is named rather than treated as disproof of coverage. The claim emphasizes the full distribution, not asserting that the radius-nine corollary alone is certainly unknown.
residual_risks: The entire 2026 Luo–Zhou–Mesnager–Sagar–Yan paper was not accessible. An exact radius-nine corollary for a potentially related extended code cannot be excluded from its main theorems; it is not known to provide the complete joint coset distribution.
The entire 2026 geometric generalization arXiv:2606.16669 could not be read; a stronger classification or implicit route is possible.
The older literature of quaternary scalar-extended Reed–Muller codes and joint coset intersections is incompletely indexed; an unobserved equivalent polynomial remains possible.
No independent scholarly novelty audit has occurred.

value.rationale: The exact joint coset-distance distribution is a natural full invariant measuring minimum simultaneous coordinate access for every pair of affine-data requests. It resolves the binary first-order four-variable instance outside previously tabulated exact generalized-radius order families, distinguishes all ten joint distances, and counts all 336 extremal two-row cosets. Unlike ordinary one-row coset weight spectra or bare radius bounds, the full polynomial gives the complete access-cost distribution. Both numerical reliability and complete finite scope are verified; it is not an arbitrary slice or an unmotivated small change.
